facts.statement: Macroplacus raeticus lived during the Rhaetian age of the upper Triassic, between 205.6 and 201.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: The type species is Macroplacus raeticus and the fossil record of this species dates back to the upper Triassic, Rhaetian age (age range: 205.6 to 201.6 million years ago).

facts.statement: Fossils of Macroplacus have been found in Germany at Hinterstein near Hindelang im Allgäu.
facts.quote: These fossils have been found in Germany, at Hinterstein near Hindelang im Allgäu.

facts.statement: The classification of Macroplacus is controversial, though it is usually placed in the Cyamodontidae or Placochelyidae.
facts.quote: The classification of Macroplacus is controversial but it is usually placed in the Cyamodontidae or in the Placochelyidae.

facts.statement: Macroplacus is a placodont reptile that looks similar to turtles but is probably related to diapsids.
facts.quote: These reptiles are placodonts, a group of animal probably related to diapsids, but that look similar to the turtles.

facts.statement: Macroplacus raeticus had a relatively flat, heavily armored body that resembled a turtle.
facts.quote: Macroplacus raeticus, the only known species, possessed a relatively flat body, quite armored and similar to that of a turtle.

facts.statement: The skull of Macroplacus was very robust and broad at the back, with a snout that narrowed toward the front.
facts.quote: The skull was very robust, broad posteriorly, with a snout narrower in the foremost part.

facts.statement: Macroplacus had exceptionally strong jaws that likely possessed powerful musculature.
facts.quote: The jaws were exceptionally strong and probably had a powerful musculature.

facts.statement: Macroplacus had round-shaped teeth on both the palate and jaws, including huge molars.
facts.quote: The teeth were present on the palate and jaw, and were round shaped, with huge molars.
The whole animal was about 1 m long.

facts.statement: Macroplacus led an amphibious lifestyle but was poorly adapted to marine environments.
facts.quote: It was an animal with an amphibious way of life, but it was little adapted to marine life.

facts.statement: Macroplacus swam slowly in shallow coastal waters to feed primarily on shellfish.
facts.quote: Like all placodonts, Macroplacus had to swim slowly in shallow water and coastal areas, in search of shellfish that made up most of its diet.

facts.statement: Macroplacus used its large, hemispheric palatal teeth to break the shells of mollusks.
facts.quote: The large palatal hemispheric teeth could break the shells of mollusks.

facts.statement: The genus Macroplacus existed from 205.7 to 201.4 million years ago during the Rhaetian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)
